messages.subject: clang on Mac
parts:
On Sunday, October 21, 2012 9:57:26 AM UTC-4, Jiqiang Guo wrote:
2. clang might not work well on old Mac say even Snow Leopard for rstan (ie, old version in Xcode), I will report some details later.

Perhaps I spoke too soon, but it raises a different question that I don't know enough about Macs to answer for sure. 

I would speculate that the average Mac user of (R)Stan is better off with a recent version of clang than with g++-4.2.x. We think we think that g++ generates somewhat faster code than clang++ does, but I don't know what we have thoroughly benchmarked that and I somewhat doubt that g++-4.2.x generates faster code than clang++ 3.x. We still have to support g++-4.2.x because that is what CRAN uses for a Mac, but I don't think that implies we should be recommending people use g++-4.2.x on a Mac.

I only know of two potential problems. One is that maybe clang is difficult to install on some Macs. Is it not a simple matter of going to 

http://llvm.org/releases/download.html

and downloading the most recent version that works on whatever cat you have? Maybe you have to put in on your $PATH? The other problem is that clang has had compatibility problems with Rcpp in the past. But Dirk claims to have hopefully resolved them in the latest version:

http://dirk.eddelbuettel.com/blog/2012/10/14#rcpp_0.9.15

So, am I overlooking something?

Ben

random seeds for the chains from the same R session.

On Sunday, October 21, 2012 10:28:51 PM UTC-4, Marcus Brubaker wrote:
We could also incorporate the process ID in the seeding or, if you want to be really clever, read some data from /dev/random to seed things.

/dev/random doesn't work on Windows, although inside R it is fairly easy to get a seed from www.random.org with the random package.

From R it might make sense to get a random draw from the R PRNG to seed the Stan PRNG.  This has the upside that the user gets the expected behaviour in their code by storing/setting the R PRNG state and, unless they want to, never need to know or worry about a separate PRNG inside stan.
Maybe we could incorporate the process ID if chain_id is not set. But I think the best route is "same seed, different chain_id, modern PRNG".

I was only suggesting using the PID when the seed wasn't specified to avoid starting multiple chains with the same seed by accident.  For instance, someone may not use the chain id (I mean, right now it's effect is purely cosmetic) and instead just launch N copies of command line stan with different out files.  If all (or even a few) of them got the same seed this would be bad.

Cheers,
Marcus
